title: STRIPPED AND THROWN IN THE PIT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped him of his robe—the ornate robe he was wearing—and they took him and threw him into the cistern. The cistern was empty; there was no water in it." - Gen 37:23-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The moment Joseph reaches his brothers, they seize him, strip off the ornate robe — the very symbol of their father's love and their own resentment — and throw him into an empty pit. In a matter of minutes, Joseph goes from a favored son in a beautiful robe to a helpless captive in a dark, dry cistern. It is a stunning, sudden fall.

Life can turn like that. One moment we are secure, and the next we find ourselves in a pit — a crisis, a betrayal, a loss we never saw coming. Joseph did nothing to deserve this; he had simply obeyed his father and come looking for his brothers. Sometimes the pit we land in is not the result of our own sin at all, but of others' cruelty.

If you find yourself in a "pit" today — a dark, low place where you feel stripped of everything and utterly alone — know that you are not the first of God's people to be there. Joseph was there. And though the story does not say it yet, God had not abandoned him in that pit. What looked like the end of Joseph's story was actually the strange beginning of God's rescue plan for many.

The pit is not the end. Hold on. The God who sees you in the darkness is already at work in ways you cannot yet see.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I ever fallen suddenly into a "pit" I did not deserve?
2. Can I trust that God has not abandoned me in the dark places?
3. How does Joseph's story give me hope in my low seasons?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I find myself in a pit — stripped, low, and alone — remind me that You have not abandoned me. You are at work even in the darkness. Help me to hold on and trust You. Amen.
